description: Rung-6c clinical MANAGEMENT as a minimum-cost regimen — the economics half of the therapy decision, the step past rung-6b's dose-feasibility (CAN it be dosed) to WHAT IS THE CHEAPEST way to deliver an already-feasible therapy. Each item renders a formulary choice as a 2-variable linear program: a required daily amount must be met by splitting it between a CHEAP formulation that is capped (limited supply / coverage) and an EXPENSIVE formulation that is uncapped. The gold ADJ program declares two scalars, one constraint per bound, and a `minimize cost` objective; the ENGINE solves the LP (simplex) and returns the optimal value, read by the existing optimize_value extractor — no harness or engine change. The reasoning and the anchoring traps: maxing the cheap form to its cap then topping up with the brand is optimal (p_cheap*C + p_brand*(R-C)); a clinician who ignores the cap under-budgets at p_cheap*R, one who reaches only for the brand over-spends at p_brand*R. Twenty scenarios across antimicrobial, anticoagulant, endocrine, biologic, antiviral, oncologic, and respiratory therapy; every price and bound is stated verbatim in the stem (no-result-literal gate holds); options are distinct dollar totals. Engine returns the correct optimum 20/20 in cached mode, zero wrong.

items.stem: A patient with MRSA bacteremia needs 30 mg/day of vancomycin. Two formulations are on the formulary: a hospital-stock generic vial costs 2 per mg but only 18 mg/day are available per period; a single-dose brand vial costs 5 per mg with no supply limit. Each formulation can supply at least 0 of its units. Using both as needed to reach the required 30 mg/day, what is the lowest total cost of the regimen?
items.program:
symbol cheap : scalar
symbol brand : scalar
constrain cheap + brand >= 30
constrain cheap <= 18
constrain cheap >= 0
constrain brand >= 0
minimize 2 * cheap + 5 * brand
